chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. Indeed, Allah loves the seekers of knowledge.'

key_terms.بُغَاةَ الْعِلْمِ: seekers of knowledge — those who actively and earnestly pursue learning
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: obligation/duty (fard) — a binding religious requirement, as opposed to a recommended act

ai.seo_question: Is seeking knowledge obligatory in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain ending at Imam al-Sadiq (AS) who quotes the Prophet (SAWAS), establishes seeking knowledge as a religious duty incumbent upon all Muslims, not merely a virtue or recommendation. The second clause reinforces this by declaring Allah's love for those who actively pursue knowledge, which in the early Islamic scholarly tradition referred both to religious sciences and the practical knowledge needed to fulfill one's duties. This saying became one of the most frequently cited prophetic traditions in Islamic educational discourse, serving as the foundational justification for the vast institutions of Islamic learning.
